articles.title: Chase Infiniti Coming-of-Age Drama ‘The Julia Set’ Sells Out for HanWay (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: HanWay Films has sold out all territories globally for coming-of-age drama “The Julia Set,” starring “One Battle After Another” breakout Chase Infiniti, following its premiere in Toronto earlier this year. As previously announced, Sony Pictures Classics acquired U.S.
body: Additional sales now negotiated by HanWay Films include Sphere (Canada), Cinesky Pictures (Airlines), MegaCom Films (Former Yugoslavia), SND (France), Vuelta Germany (Germany), The Film Group (Greece), Synapse Distribution (Latin America), Front Row (Middle East), Kino Świat (Poland), Nos Lusomundo Audiovisuais (Portugal), Shaw Renters (Singapore) and Bir Film (Turkey).

Directed by Niki Byrne, “The Julia Set” follows math prodigy Julia Fischer (Infiniti), who is recruited into an elite prep course culminating in the most punishing exam in mathematics. At the same time, she begins to fall for her charismatic teaching assistant Pascal (Christopher Briney). As Pascal crumbles under the weight of his overbearing father Aleksander’s (Jason Isaacs) suffocating expectations, it is Pascal’s mother, Anne (Gillian Anderson), who helps Julia recognize and seize a moment of opportunity that will help to define her future.
The film also stars Nina Hoss, Carmen Ejogo, Chloe Bailey, Nico Hiraga, Liz Lin and Alex Dillard.

articles.title: ‘Wolfenstein 3’ in Development at Xbox’s MachineGames
articles.summary: “Wolfenstein 3” is in the works at Xbox’s Machine Games. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the news Thursday amid Xbox’s 25th anniversary celebration, sharing on X: “Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames.
body: First launched in 1981 by Muse Software, the “Wolfenstein” video game franchise is set in an alternate history World War II. There are more than a dozen games in the series with the two most recent installments being reboots developed by MachineGames in partnership with publisher Bethesda Softworks: 2014’s “Wolfenstein: The New Order” and 2017’s “Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus.”
“Wolfenstein 3” will mark the first game in the franchise to be developed by MachineGames under Xbox ownership following Microsoft’s acquisition of parent company ZeniMax Media in March 2021.

articles.summary: As most theater fans already know, “Oh, Mary!,” which is as hysterical as it is ahistorical, is the story of possibly unhinged presidential spouse Mary Todd Lincoln, and her thwarted aspirations to escape life in the parlors of the White House for a career in show business.
body: Sometimes, when we do a piece about a play coming in, we say something about how we’ll be “helping spread the news.” It might sound silly to say that about this show, though — ust about everyone in L.A. knows that it’s coming.
Well, that’s because there are so many flags on flag poles. It’s like a fascist “Oh, Mary!” state with all of those “Oh, Mary!” flags everywhere.

The tour has been in San Francisco, Portland and Seattle on its way to the Ahmanson. Assuming you must have come out west to see how it’s doing at at least one of those stops, any thoughts on how it’s working as a touring show?

So many of us are curious about how it will feel because you’ve got such a perfect jewel box environment there in New York. But you feel like, from what you’ve been able to see, you get a similar reaction?

articles.title: Savannah Guthrie Extends Contract With NBC News
articles.summary: Savannah Guthrie’s tenure at “Today” still has a lot of tomorrow in it. Guthrie has extended her current deal with NBC News, according to a person familiar with the matter, a move that will keep her at the desk of the network’s flagship “Today” program at a time when the show has surged ahead of
body: Savannah Guthrie ‘s tenure at “Today” still has a lot of tomorrow in it.

Guthrie, however, enjoys tremendous standing at NBCUniversal. She is widely seen as a guiding force at “Today,” a signature program she co-anchors with Craig Melvin. While the morning-news audience is not what it once was decades ago, viewership is still seen as devoted and significant. The first two hours of “Today” — watched by around 3 million viewers each weekday — generated nearly $203.5 million in advertising in 2025, according to Guideline, a tracker of ad spending. Add the 9 a.m. and 10 a.m. hours to the mix, and NBC nabbed around $315.4 million from the weekday editions of the program.

She also plays a key role in other parts of coverage, including the network’s recent Election Night that was the most-watched among the traditional TV-news outlets. What’s more, Guthrie is the host of a new show based on the popular “Wordle” game from The New York Times slated to debut in coming months on NBC. “She’s fantastic,” says Jimmy Fallon, whose Electric Hot Dog production company is one of the backers of the program, during a recent interview with Variety.
points: Savannah Guthrie’s tenure at “Today” still has a lot of tomorrow in it.

articles.title: Ebenezer review – Johnny Depp’s Scrooge tries to exorcise ghosts of business past
articles.summary: The latest film version of the Dickens classic A Christmas Carol is decent enough, though its star is rather better as the legendary miser before redemption arrives. Here for lovers of Dickens – and fans of subtext – is an unexpectedly watchable new movie version of A Christmas Carol starring a…
body: In fact, screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern and director Ti West have put together a perfectly serviceable, faithful adaptation – a tradaptation, if you will – of Dickens’s masterpiece about the hideous old miser saved from damnation on Christmas Eve by the appearance of three Christmas ghosts, from yuletides past, present and future. It sticks to the accepted narrative beats and more or less all the familiar episodes, but with a few twists.

There is a witty and ingenious new prologue sequence in which Scrooge’s equally grumpy partner Jacob Marley, played by Ian McKellen, is still alive, going into a full Stadler-and-Waldorf double-act with his old colleague. (Wait – did The Muppet Christmas Carol inspire this?) And West shows us his scary-movie style by having that scene coming to a disturbing close with a kettle’s eerie whistle as it comes to the boil.
points: The latest film version of the Dickens classic A Christmas Carol is decent enough, though its star is rather better as the legendary miser before redemption arrives.

articles.title: ‘Goats are good. They listen’: the herder who defeated Montenegro’s military – and can identify her cows’ herby burps
articles.summary: To Hold a Mountain tells the incredible story of a woman whose way of life was threatened when she heard her pastures were set to become a Nato training zone. The star of To Hold a Mountain is having trouble with her goats, which keep escaping.
body: “You have to take care of them because they are always searching for their paths,” says Gara, whose Montenegrin is translated into English by Biljana Tutorov, the joint writer-director of the stunning film about Gara’s life in the mountains of Sinjajevina. “But the goats are good, especially when they know the shepherdess. I’m a good shepherdess. They listen to me.”

People listen to Gara too, as Tutorov and her partner and co-writer/director Petar Glomazić discovered eight years ago. Their epic commitment to filming this pastoralist community, whose way of life is threatened, has been rewarded: To Hold a Mountain has swept up prizes on the festival circuit after winning the grand jury prize for world cinema documentary at Sundance earlier this year.

The film-makers first met Gara when she spoke at a rally against the government’s plans to turn a swath of the mountains into a Nato military training and weapons testing facility. “Somebody had to say something, and all men were reluctant,” says Glomazić. “And then one woman jumped on the white horse, took the megaphone, and made an incredible speech. And that was Gara.”

articles.title: Tyrese Gibson to Star in Sports Drama ‘Under the Boards’ From ‘Home Alone’ Producer Scott Rosenfelt (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The feature is set to begin production next year and takes inspiration from the real-life championship run for Atlantic City High School's basketball team.
body: Tyrese Gibson is looking to bring an inspirational story of high school basketball triumph to the big screen.

The actor, known for the Fast and Furious franchise, is set to star in writer-director Scott Rosenfelt’s sports drama Under the Boards, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. The indie film is expected to begin production in February.

Rosenfelt, who helms the movie from his own script, serves as producer alongside Salomé Breziner. Schafer, Gibson and T’Shaun Barrett serve as executive producers, while Debby Schafer co-produces. Jim Schafer, whose path helped inspire the project, is married to Rosenfelt’s cousin, and the casting process is underway to cast the actor who will portray Schafer.

“This film belongs to Atlantic City,” says Rosenfelt. “Tyrese understands that a coach like Gene is part preacher, part politician and part father to every kid on that bench. He is going to bring that whole community to life.”

articles.title: You can see everything on this list: the 20 most jaw-dropping documentaries – ranked!
articles.summary: Ahead of the UK release of Nathan Fielder’s hotly anticipated Elizabeth Holmes film, we count down the most shocking and affecting true stories ever committed to cinema.
body: A 50-second dispatch from daily life blew the whistle on the approaching juggernaut of cinema and its unbeatable horsepower of verisimilitude. But if we must be strictly factual about the iconic Lumière brothers’ short, the anecdote about audience members fleeing their seats in fear of being crushed by the oncoming locomotive probably never happened.

The dramatic re-enactment is the car chase of the documentary industry: a crude way of keeping our attention. But by using rotoscoped animation, Keith Maitland’s riveting account of the 1966 mass shooting at the University of Texas completely revitalises the re-enactment as part of the documentary toolkit. It leaves us prone under the killer’s crosshairs with the emotional immediacy of a thriller and an oddly elegiac comedown.

articles.title: Victorian Psycho review – Maika Monroe has a blast in unsteady horror romp
articles.summary: The It Follows and Longlegs star tears into the role of a murderous governess in this hit-and-miss adaptation of Virginia Feito’s gory novel. It’s not that hard to figure out why a lower-class woman toiling away in Victorian England would be so easily driven to violently murder everyone around her.
body: As Winifred Notty (Maika Monroe) fills the frame in Victorian Psycho, heading to a new job as governess for a rich family, it’s easy to be on her side. Even as her murderous impulses start to rear their head, they’re made somewhat understandable, although Winifred isn’t just a woman reacting to the various injustices of the time – she’s one responding to a demon within her, a darkness she has chosen to embrace rather than resist. Darkness is her friend, a protection against harm, and a way to possess some sort of control in a world that has denied her any of it.

The actor has become known as a bit of a scream queen (an all too easily crowned title these days) ever since she broke out in It Follows, but despite roles in hits such as Longlegs and Watcher, she’s never really been afforded that much to do beyond looking petrified. Maybe that’s why it feels like she has so much more to give and prove here, really tearing into a character that requires her to do the petrifying. It’s not just the malevolent soundscape that makes it seem like there is an evil within her but Monroe’s unearthly contortions, an all-in, all-body performance that avoids slipping into histrionic silliness.

articles.title: Duran Duran drummer quits band due to tinnitus
articles.summary: Roger Taylor says his condition has been getting steadily worse, and he must now "listen to my body and my doctors".
body: Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor said he will leave the band due to his worsening tinnitus.
The 66-year-old said his condition has been getting steadily worse, leading to him making one of his hardest decisions to quit the band.

The group, made up of Simon Le Bon, keyboardist Nick Rhodes and guitarist John Taylor, said his decision came after "careful consideration and medical advice", which said that "protecting his hearing and long-term health must now come first".

Taylor, who left the band in 1985 before returning in 2001, said: "Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I'll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they've shown us over the years.

articles.title: Are Audiences Ready for a Johnny Depp Career Comeback?
articles.summary: After years away from studio features, the star returns to the box office fray with Paramount's 'Ebenezer.' Analysts are taking note of his lack of introspective press moments on the tour: "It's a clever — if obvious — strategy."
body: For many onlookers, it likely seems fitting that Johnny Depp returns to the big screen this weekend to play a man haunted by past mistakes.

That is set to change with Ebenezer, as director Ti West ‘s feature adaptation of Charles Dickens’ classic A Christmas Carol hits theaters Friday. Paramount Pictures, which greenlit the film shortly after David Ellison’s Skydance Media acquired the studio two years ago, releases Ebenezer in more than 3,500 North American locations and projects an opening of $20 million domestically, along with another $20 million internationally. Such a turnout is likely to place it No. 1 at the North American box office, as the other major release for the frame is David Leitch’s How to Rob a Bank, eyeing a domestic launch in the high single digits against a $40 million budget.
